title: Learn
description: Learn how to validate data before it is accepted by an algorithm. This section focuses on thinking through what makes input valid or invalid.

blocks.text: Input validation is the process of checking that data entered into a program is acceptable before the program uses it.
In Paper 2 pseudocode questions, validation usually means repeating input until the value meets the required condition.

slides.title: Validation problems usually ask you to:

blocks.title: Validation problems usually ask you to:
items: Check whether the value is valid
Display an error message if it is invalid
Continue only when valid data has been entered

blocks.title: Core thinking question:
items: Should the loop continue while the value is invalid?
What message should be shown for invalid input?

slides.title: Validate a mark
slides.problem: Input a mark. The mark must be between 0 and 100 inclusive.
slides.code:
DECLARE mark : INTEGER

INPUT mark

WHILE mark < 0 OR mark > 100
    OUTPUT "Invalid mark"
    INPUT mark
ENDWHILE
slides.explanation: The valid range is 0 to 100. The loop continues while the mark is outside this range.

slides.title: Try It
slides.task: Write pseudocode to input an age. The age must be between 1 and 120 inclusive.
slides.expectedAnswer:
DECLARE age : INTEGER

INPUT age

WHILE age < 1 OR age > 120
    OUTPUT "Invalid age"
    INPUT age
ENDWHILE

markScheme.criterion: Correct invalid condition for values below 1
Correct invalid condition for values above 120
Uses clear invalid message or re-entry structure

blocks.text: A common mistake is writing the condition for valid data instead of invalid data.
For a WHILE validation loop, the condition usually describes what is invalid, because the loop repeats while the input is wrong.

slides.title: Valid Condition vs Invalid Condition: Code pattern

blocks.text:
WHILE value is invalid
    OUTPUT "Invalid"
    INPUT value
ENDWHILE

slides.title: Validate a menu option
slides.problem: Input a menu option. The option must be 1, 2, 3 or 4.
slides.code:
DECLARE option : INTEGER

INPUT option

WHILE option < 1 OR option > 4
    OUTPUT "Invalid option"
    INPUT option
ENDWHILE
slides.explanation: The valid options are 1 to 4. The invalid condition is option < 1 OR option > 4.

slides.title: Try It
slides.task: Write pseudocode to input a level. The level must be 1, 2 or 3.
slides.expectedAnswer:
DECLARE level : INTEGER

INPUT level

WHILE level < 1 OR level > 3
    OUTPUT "Invalid level"
    INPUT level
ENDWHILE

blocks.text: REPEAT UNTIL can also be used for validation because it always allows input to happen at least once.

slides.title: Validation Using REPEAT UNTIL: Code pattern

blocks.text:
REPEAT
    INPUT value
UNTIL value is valid
With REPEAT UNTIL, the condition is usually the valid condition, because the loop stops when the data is valid.

slides.title: Validate password length
slides.problem: Input a password. It must be at least 8 characters long.
slides.code:
DECLARE password : STRING

REPEAT
    INPUT password
    IF LENGTH(password) < 8 THEN
        OUTPUT "Password too short"
    ENDIF
UNTIL LENGTH(password) >= 8
slides.explanation: The loop stops only when the password length is at least 8.

slides.title: Try It
slides.task: Write pseudocode to input a username. The username must be at least 5 characters long.
slides.expectedAnswer:
DECLARE username : STRING

REPEAT
    INPUT username
    IF LENGTH(username) < 5 THEN
        OUTPUT "Username too short"
    ENDIF
UNTIL LENGTH(username) >= 5

markScheme.criterion: Uses REPEAT UNTIL or equivalent validation loop
Loop stops only when username is valid
